messages:
sam: Heads-up — eu-west embeddings/rerank pool has been sitting at queue_depth > 120 for ~10m, several client 429s observed. Can we triage?

ops-bot: [ALERT] lane=eu-west1-embeddings queue_depth=128 inflight=96 p95_latency=1.92s reason=burst_rerank

maria: Wait which pool exactly — rerank and embeddings are on the same GPU pool right now? @sam

sam: Yes looks like a shared small-model pool serving both embed + rerank. Rerank traffic spiked and is crowding out embedding requests.

alex: We need an explicit admission_signal metric from the admission controller (NORMAL | BACKPRESSURE | SHEDDING) so the router can start degrading gracefully (route to dedicated lanes / reduce concurrency).

devin: Also let's decide on 429 vs 503. 429 triggers some SDK retry loops badly. I think 503 + Retry-After is safer for backpressure.

jun: Short-term mitigation: lower rerank.max_concurrency per-worker from 12 -> 6 and enable per-tenant fairshare. That should free ~20-30 slots for embedding bursts.

lisa: Quick config sketch for admission controller (apply as canary):

```yaml
admission: 
  lanes:
    embeddings-eu-west:
      capacity: 120
      algorithm: leaky_bucket
      max_inflight: 96
      soft_threshold: 0.8   # start BACKPRESSURE at 80%
      hard_threshold: 1.0   # SHEDDING at 100%
      backpressure_response: 503
      retry_after_secs: 2
      per_tenant_shares: true

    rerank-eu-west-fallback:
      capacity: 40
      model_white_list: ["rerank-quant-v2"]
      route_on_signal: BACKPRESSURE
```

maria: Nice. For the backpressure_response we should include a small JSON payload explaining degradation (so SDKs can surface friendly UI).

alex: Also emit lane.admission_signal and lane.queue_depth as metrics to datadog and create alerts on sustained BACKPRESSURE > 5m.

devin: Ops playbook idea: if queue_depth>100 for 10m -> 1) reduce rerank concurrency 2) spin up dedicated small pool (if capacity) 3) enable rerank fallback routing.

sam: Note: fallback to quantized rerank reduces topK accuracy by ~3% on our eval. Good trade for best-effort customers but we must tag tenants who opt-in.

jun: Implementation notes: admission controller should expose an HTTP /v1/signal endpoint returning {signal: "BACKPRESSURE", reason: "cpu/queue"} so the router can decide. Avoid embedding decision logic in router.

lisa: I'll open the infra PR for the config and a small endpoint in admission controller. Can we schedule a canary window at 02:00 UTC?

maria: I'll draft runbook steps and the customer opt-in flag. Putting a link in infra PR. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: [INCIDENT] INC-2026-0818 created (priority=P2) — queue saturation eu-west embeddings. Ping #oncall for remediation.

sam: thanks. Oncall — can someone apply the temp throttle and monitor for 15m?

alex: I'll apply the per-worker concurrency patch as canary in eu-west and wire the admission_signal metric.

devin: I'll update the SDK guidance to treat 503+Retry-After as backpressure and avoid aggressive retry.

maria: After we stabilize let's discuss longer-term: split pools per workload (embed-only, rerank-only), and quota-based admission with tenant credits.

sam: Agreed. For now tactical actions in order: emit signal -> router read -> temp throttle -> fallback lane.

lisa: created PR https://git.internal/r/infr/ctl/merge/789 with config + unit tests.

sam: Great — keep updates in this thread.

(emoji reactions: alex :thumbsup:, maria :rocket:, jun :eyes:)
